generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Copy an existing parent primary-key value; for nullable FKs include NULL rows (share ~5-10%) and rows referencing parents that have no children.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real in the observed range; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side; never NULL for NOT NULL columns.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Pick from a small pool of 3-8 distinct short strings; include near-variants (case changes, truncations, one-character edits) of listed equality literals; allow NULL only for nullable columns.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Generate plausible person/club names; allow duplicates on DISTINCT-targeted columns (20-50% duplicate share) and near-variants.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For every nullable column, at least one NULL row per instance; share follows compact DB (mostly 0% observed, so use 0-10%).

issues.summary: Semantic rule competition.Competition_type IN ('Friendly','Tournament') conflicts with enum_variants near-variants.
issues.evidence: specification.py defines enums[competition.Competition_type]=['Friendly','Tournament'] AND enum_variants containing 'Tament','tament','name','NAME','rn','RN','rnam','RNAM'. EnumSampler emits variants with prob 0.15, so generated rows routinely hold values violating the stated CHECK-style rule. The semantic_rules say Competition_type IN ('Friendly','Tournament'), but the spec also lists the alternate literals as targets (atomic ops comparison_boundary). These are contradictory: a value like 'Tament' is not in the semantic domain.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify whether the near-variant literals are only for literal POOL coverage (used in queries, not necessarily inserted into rows) versus inserted values. If inserted, the semantic rule must be relaxed (e.g., only non-NULL operands and treat rule as 'holds when not FALSE' with the domain being a soft target), otherwise EnumSampler should not emit out-of-domain variants for this column. As-is the two spec statements are inconsistent.

issues.summary: Formulas use spec/keys but the Generation specification JSON uses different key names (formulas/op/of vs semantic_rules_and_formulas); _apply_formulas relies on instantiated SPEC format, not the provided JSON.
issues.evidence: instance._apply_formulas expects spec['formulas'][key]['op']=='sum' with 'of'. The provided Generation specification JSON has 'semantic_rules_and_formulas' with a 'formula' string 'Total = Gold + Silver + Bronze' and no 'formulas' dict. When load_specification(root) loads an external specification.json in the raw Generation-spec format, _apply_formulas finds no 'formulas' key and the derivation is silently skipped; only the built-in SPEC (with correct 'formulas') works. Confirmed by specification.py: SPEC is a hand-translated internal structure distinct from the supplied JSON.
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) guarantee the runtime loads the internal SPEC-derived structure (not the raw Generation-spec JSON) and document that specification.json is a different schema, or (b) adapt _apply_formulas/loaders to parse the supplied semantic_rules_and_formulas string format. Do not leave a silent no-op for Total derivation when an external spec file is supplied.

issues.summary: Some nullable columns get 0 NULLs in generated rows (club.name, club.Region, player.Points, etc.).
issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback: 'club.Region: NULL 0/49', 'club.Start_year: NULL 0/49', 'club.name: NULL 0/49', 'player.Points: NULL 0/60', etc. Per instructions item 7 this is noted but does not block a pass; these are columns not in null_targets. The NULL rule requires at least one NULL per nullable column that is a null_target; column with NULL 0/n that are not null_targets is allowed by interface note.
issues.requested_revision: Optional: include these columns in null_targets for full interface-rule compliance per column, but not blocking.
